item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00336","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C15","C23","C12"],"selected_candidate_label":"C15","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C15 is a direct and material drafting precursor. Written only days earlier to the same recipient about the same requested loyalty files, it supplies the child’s central sequence of arguments: disclosure would impair FBI effectiveness, endanger confidential informants, injure innocent persons because files contain unverified allegations, and damage the loyalty program. It also supplies the proposed alternative of an independent Loyalty Review Board review. C23 provides the underlying confidentiality directive and subpoena-refusal machinery, but C15 much more closely supplies the child’s actual language and organization. C12 has only a general separation-of-powers resemblance.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The disclosure of these files would seriously prejudice the future effectiveness and usefulness of the Federal Bureau of Investigation as an investigative agency; the embarrassment, and even danger, to those who have given confidential information cannot be overemphasized.","parent_excerpt":"These three elements--the serious prejudice to the effectiveness of the Federal Bureau of Investigation as an investigative agency, the resulting embarrassment and danger to confidential informants, and injustice and unfairness to innocent individuals-led me to the inescapable conclusion...","explanation":"The child restates C15’s distinctive three-part rationale in closely matching language."},{"child_excerpt":"The investigative files of the Federal Bureau of Investigation do not contain proven information alone. They include any unverified charges and allegations, leads and suspicions.","parent_excerpt":"Investigative reports include leads and suspicions, and sometimes even the statements of malicious or misinformed people.","explanation":"Both use the distinctive point that investigative files contain unverified leads and suspicions, so disclosure would injure innocent people."},{"child_excerpt":"I have asked the bipartisan Loyalty Review Board to make an independent review of the loyalty cases before your Subcommittee.","parent_excerpt":"I am, therefore, asking Mr. Seth Richardson, Chairman of the Loyalty Review Board, to have the Board arrange for a complete and detailed review...of the cases in which charges of disloyalty have been made before your Subcommittee.","explanation":"The child carries forward the same administrative substitute for producing the confidential files."}]}
